lyric_idea: Chorus: "If someone tells me one more time / 'Enjoy your youth,' I'm gonna cry". Advice to young people that AI undercuts: 'learn to code' vs AI coding agents writing most code; entry-level hiring collapse for new graduates (2025-2026).

candidates.text: From: (Learn to code) –> (Join big tech company) –> (Build confidence) –> (Understand customers) –> (Become a founder)
candidates.speaker_or_outlet: SignalFire, State of Tech Talent Report 2026 (report text, not a person's quote)
candidates.date: 2026-06-22 (deck manifest date; the live page fetched 2026-10-10 shows no date)
candidates.verified_how: Opened the live report page on 2026-10-10 and copied the line verbatim. The same page says: 'New grad/entry-level hiring has collapsed further: down roughly 65% at the Tech Majors* and down ~76% at early stage startups* compared to 2019.' Deck source: assets/research/work/manifest.json, swe-signalfire-* items; tools/slides_work.js juniorSlide.
candidates.why_it_fits: Puts 'learn to code' on screen as the old career path, with an arrow to 'Become a founder'. The report calls the old ladder obsolete, which is the lyric's point about advice to the young.
candidates.caveat: The same report says the 'AI Code Apocalypse' 'has failed to materialize' for engineers, and engineering hiring at Tech Majors is down only ~11%. Do not caption it as AI replacing coders. For a phone, trim the middle steps with an ellipsis ('From: (Learn to code) –> … –> (Become a founder)') rather than rewording.

candidates.text: employment of young workers (ages 22–25) in AI-exposed occupations now stands 19% below where it would be had it kept pace with that of their less-exposed peers; experienced workers show no comparable gap.
candidates.speaker_or_outlet: Erik Brynjolfsson, Bharat Chandar, Ruyu Chen, Stanford Digital Economy Lab, 'Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence'
candidates.verified_how: Viewed the local chart PNG: the 'Early Career 1 (22-25)' line ends near 0.8 of its late-2022 level, while 'Mid-Career 2 (41-49)' ends near 1.2. Fetched the paper text on 2026-10-10 and matched the 19% sentence (Fact 2, section 2.2). Deck source: manifest item swe-stanford-canaries, cropped from p.62.
candidates.why_it_fits: Youth is the subject of 'Enjoy your youth'. This is the paper's 'canary' finding on young workers, shown next to the age split.
candidates.caveat: The paper calls this descriptive, not causal, and finds no economy-wide displacement. The 0.8 on the chart is headcount, not the 19% counterfactual gap; do not merge the two numbers. The deck label '−20%' is a rounding of the chart, so prefer the paper's 19%.

candidates.text: Once Seen as a Sure Thing, Computer Science Has Lost 53,000 Majors
candidates.speaker_or_outlet: The Chronicle of Higher Education (Jacquelyn Elias)
candidates.verified_how: Viewed the local screenshot of the rendered page: headline, byline and 'August 27, 2026' are visible. The article body is paywalled (403 on fetch), so the 53,000 figure rests on the headline alone.
candidates.why_it_fits: 'Sure thing' is the same 'safe bet' the advice to young people pointed to. Fortune (2026-08-06) makes the same point: CS 'was considered one of higher education's safest bets'.
candidates.caveat: Headline-only figure. Do not state a breakdown of the 53,000 that the body would need to support.

candidates.text: Google CEO says 75% of company’s new code is AI-generated
candidates.speaker_or_outlet: Semafor (Tom Chivers); primary source Sundar Pichai, Google Cloud Next '26
candidates.local_path: /home/user/poster/ai-safety-presentation/assets/research/work/swe-semafor-google75.png (listed in the deck manifest; not opened by me)
candidates.verified_how: Opened the Semafor page on 2026-10-10. The headline matches verbatim, and the dek reads: 'Google chief Sundar Pichai said 75% of the company’s new code is AI-generated. In 2024 that figure was 25%, rising to 50% last fall.' The Google blog line ('75% of all new code at Google is now AI-generated and approved by engineers') comes from the deck manifest notes; I did not open the Google blog.
candidates.why_it_fits: The cleanest echo of the 'learn to code' half of the lyric: the job advice is 'learn to code', and the headline says AI now writes most of the new code.
candidates.caveat: Google-reported, self-reported figure. Quote the headline exactly; the page says 'Google chief' in the body, 'Google CEO' in the headline.
